titulo: Praise that reaches the kitchen, and the sentence that gets it fixed
subtitulo: The specific compliment brings the cook out; the calm, factual sentence gets the dish changed
cena: The dish was genuinely wonderful, the one before it was cold, and you have about ten seconds to do something useful with either fact.
frasePiso: Name the thing. A compliment with a noun in it travels to the kitchen; a complaint with a fact in it gets acted on.
decisao: elogiar nomeando o prato e reclamar nomeando o fato, em vez de dizer 'tudo ótimo' e depois escrever uma avaliação ruim de casa

steps.pt: Two sentences, opposite jobs, same rule: name the thing. Vague praise dies at the table and vague complaints get an apology instead of a fix.
Praise first. Tutto buono is polite noise. Name the dish and it becomes a message someone will actually repeat.

steps.es: La pasta era buonissima, complimenti al cuoco.
steps.pinyin: la PAS-ta EH-ra bwo-NEES-see-ma, kom-plee-MEN-tee al KWO-ko
steps.pt: The pasta was outstanding, compliments to the cook.
steps.tts: La pasta era buonissima, complimenti al cuoco.

steps.promptPt: Praise one dish by name and send it to the kitchen. Speak now.
steps.es: La pasta era buonissima, complimenti al cuoco.
steps.pinyin: la PAS-ta EH-ra bwo-NEES-see-ma, kom-plee-MEN-tee al KWO-ko
steps.pt: The pasta was outstanding, compliments to the cook.

steps.acao: Stay at the table. The cook may actually come out, and leaving mid-compliment is the one rude move here.
steps.es: Glielo dico subito. È mia madre che cucina.
steps.pt: I'll tell her right away. It's my mother who cooks.
steps.tts: Glielo dico subito. È mia madre che cucina.

steps.pt: Buonissimo, ottimo, squisito. Any of the three is stronger than very good, and all three are ordinary words here.

steps.promptPt: Praise the place rather than the plate. Speak now.

steps.pt: Now the complaint. State the fact, no adjectives, no apology. Scusi, plus what is wrong, and then stop talking.

steps.promptPt: The dish arrived cold. Say only that. Speak now.

steps.es: Mi dispiace tantissimo, glielo cambio subito.
steps.pt: I'm terribly sorry, I'll change it right away.
steps.tts: Mi dispiace tantissimo, glielo cambio subito.

steps.pt: That worked because there was a fact in it. Adding it is a shame or I am so sorry to bother you gives them nothing to act on.

steps.promptPt: Wrong dish entirely. Say what you ordered instead. Speak now.
steps.es: Scusi, io avevo ordinato il pesce.
steps.pinyin: SKOO-zee, EE-o a-VE-vo or-dee-NA-to eel PE-she
steps.pt: Sorry, I had ordered the fish.
steps.tts: Scusi, io avevo ordinato il pesce.

steps.promptPt: The glass is chipped. Ask for another, using the frame from B14. Speak now.
steps.es: Mi porta un altro bicchiere, per favore?
steps.pinyin: mee POR-ta oon AL-tro beek-kee-EH-re per fa-VO-re
steps.pt: Could you bring me another glass, please?
steps.tts: Mi porta un altro bicchiere, per favore?

steps.promptPt: It has been forty minutes. Ask about it without accusing anyone. Speak now.
steps.pt: Sorry, is it still a long wait?

steps.promptPt: They fixed it immediately. Close the loop so it does not stay awkward. Speak now.
steps.pt: Thank you, very kind. No problem at all.

steps.promptPt: Say you will come back — the strongest compliment there is. Speak now.

steps.es: La pasta era buonissima, complimenti al cuoco. Scusi, questo è freddo. Grazie, gentilissimo.
steps.pinyin: la PAS-ta EH-ra bwo-NEES-see-ma kom-plee-MEN-tee al KWO-ko. SKOO-zee KWES-to eh FRED-do. GRA-tsee-eh jen-tee-LEES-see-mo
steps.pt: Shadow praise, complaint, and the close that keeps the room warm.
steps.tts: La pasta era buonissima, complimenti al cuoco. Scusi, questo è freddo. Grazie, gentilissimo.

steps.pt: I07 done. Name the dish to praise it, name the fact to fix it, and close warmly either way.

secoes.corpo: It is a fixed phrase and it does exactly what it says: the waiter relays it. In a family-run place the cook may come out, which is why the compliment is worth making before you ask for the bill rather than on the way out.
Questo è freddo. Avevo ordinato il pesce. Manca ancora molto. Three complaints, no adjectives, no story about how long you have been travelling. The shorter the sentence, the faster the fix.

Padding a complaint with apology buries the fact the other person needs. It also signals that you expect resistance, which invites it. A flat, warm, factual sentence is read as normal rather than as confrontation.
Torniamo domani outranks any adjective. Places that feed the same people every week measure their work in return visits, not in reviews.

permissao: You are allowed to send a dish back. Scusi, questo è freddo is a normal sentence in an Italian restaurant, it is heard as information rather than as an attack, and the version where you eat it cold and write a bad review from the hotel helps nobody, including you.
espelho: Anyone who has eaten a wrong order at home rather than flag it, then complained about it in the car, already knows the reflex. It is not about Italian — it is the belief that saying something makes you difficult, which is exactly backwards.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You praise a dish and the waiter disappears, then returns with the person who cooked it, who stands at your table waiting.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I have caused a scene and now I have to perform enthusiasm.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: In family-run places the compliment is passed on literally and the cook coming out is the reply. It is a small ceremony of acknowledgement, not an audit of how much you meant it.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Repeat the specific thing — the dish, the one element you noticed — and say grazie. Twenty seconds is a complete exchange.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You end up in a real conversation with the person whose work you just enjoyed, which is most of what the module is for.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not in a large or busy restaurant with a professional brigade, where the compliment stays with the waiter and nobody is going to leave the pass for it.
